newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma and forwards come off highs, FRNs bid.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma and forwards come off highs, FRNs bid.

text.p: Greek depos steadied, one-year forex forwards slipped from morning highs to settle lower and 2004 FRN buying interest boosted prices in late trade, dealers said.
"Depos are holding, but one-year forex swaps have eased 20 pips (forward points) after climbing 40 pips to 1220 earlier on," dealers said.
They attributed the moves in forex forwards to easing dollar rates, profit-taking and prior mispricing.

The Bank of Greece drained 200 billion drachmas ($756.1 million) of 14-day depos through a competitive interest rate tender on Wednesday at an average rate of 11.95 percent. Interest rates ranged from 11.78 percent to 11.97 percent
Bond dealers reported strong interest from abroad for seven-year FRNs due 2004 that took prices higher to 102.10 from 101.75 at open.
The mark was quoted at 156.97/07 from Wednesday's 156.830 fix, the dollar at 264.76/86 drachmas from 265.570 and the Ecu at 304.39/49 from 304.050 drachmas.
Ecu/drachmas was bid early on hitting 304.60 but has yielded ground since then and currently trades at 304.01/06, said a forex dealer at a foreign bank.
